laterChanges: Act 174 of the 2026 Fiscal Session raises the cap to $675 beginning with assessment year 2026, normally collected in 2027. It does not replace the $600 cap for assessment year 2025.
name: Arkansas
overview: The homestead credit reduces qualifying homeowners' property-tax liability without an income test.

programs.name: Homestead Property Tax Credit
programs.maximumBenefit: Lesser of $600 and qualifying homestead tax for assessment year 2025, normally collected in 2026.
programs.formulaSummary: Nonrefundable bill credit equal to the lesser of qualified homestead real-property ad valorem tax before this credit and the assessment-year cap. Any unused cap is not a cash payment.
programs.application: Register the homestead and establish eligibility with the county assessor. Section 26-26-1118(b)(3), as amended by Act 1268 of 2005, bars the credit after October 10 of the year after assessment. Later codification of this subsection remains unverified.
eligibilityNotes: Applies to a qualifying owner-occupied homestead.
Assessment year and bill-payment year differ; the assessment-year cap governs even if payment is early or late.

Section 26-26-1118(b)(4), as amended by Act 1268 of 2005, requires the parcel to qualify as a homestead before January 1 of the year after assessment. Later codification of this subsection remains unverified.
County parcel qualification, valid registration, annual property history and qualified pre-credit tax determine eligibility and amount.
interactions: Assessment limitations and disability/veteran exemptions are separate forms of relief.
A person claiming the disabled-veteran property-tax exemption cannot also claim this credit; veteran status alone is not the exclusion.

programs.name: Real estate taxes in Arkansas itemized deductions
programs.ageRule: No age test on this deduction.
programs.incomeDefinition: Arkansas itemizers deduct eligible real estate taxes from Arkansas adjusted gross income as part of total itemized deductions.
programs.incomeLimits: No income limit on eligible real estate taxes for this deduction.
programs.maximumBenefit: Eligible real estate taxes paid. The deduction reduces taxable income.
programs.formulaSummary: Arkansas includes eligible real estate taxes paid on owned nonbusiness property in itemized deductions without applying the federal combined state and local tax cap.
programs.application: Enter eligible taxes on Form AR3 line 5 and use Form AR3 to calculate the total itemized deductions on Form AR1000F.
eligibilityNotes: Exclude special assessments, levy taxes and property you use for business.
interactions: Arkansas lets filers choose itemized deductions separately from their federal deduction. The standard deduction or low-income tax table can affect the final benefit.
programs.programYear: 2025 Arkansas income-tax return, based on taxes paid in 2025.

researchNotes: Act 330 of 2025 raised the assessment-year-2025 credit to $600.
The assessment-year-2025 credit normally appears on the 2026 bill; the assessment-year-2026 credit normally appears on the 2027 bill.

The statutory caps are $425 for assessment 2023, $500 for assessment 2024, $600 for assessment 2025 and $675 from assessment 2026. A tax paid during 2025 ordinarily relates to assessment 2024 and its $500 cap.
